nodes.label: Checkpoint ABI, portable actor and continuation boundaries
nodes.norm_label: checkpoint abi, portable actor and continuation boundaries
nodes.rationale: 100D/2D, 103D/1D v1, 103D/1D v2 and 23D/2D SAC are distinct contracts. Resumable bundles preserve learner/replay/identity state but not exact Gazebo/contact/RNG episode state. The current portable actor enforces two outputs and generic shadow expects its base ABI; common103_v2 needs a matching export/adapter.

nodes.label: Reported Wheel SysID
nodes.rationale: Identification fits aggregate final-request-to-reported-wheel delay, lag, and gain with nominal geometry and a common receipt clock. residual_sysid.py requires at least three complete sessions, nonempty whole-session holdout, SI units, clocks, and provenance. These software gates do not establish statistical sufficiency, calibrated body dynamics, or physical channel mapping.

nodes.label: Hardware Inventory Audit
nodes.rationale: hardware_audit inventories graph endpoints, packages, allowed read-only parameters, TF, timestamps, observed rates, and power evidence. It uses the actual driver domain/overlay. A node or package name does not prove physical connectivity, installed TF does not verify mounting, and absent warnings do not establish adequate power.

nodes.label: Raw Session Bundle
nodes.rationale: The session bundle retains manifest, session metadata, actual collection/QoS configuration, optional signal mapping, raw CDR bag and metadata, recorder/audit logs, audit graph/samples, power timeline, and hashes. Failures and spikes remain with the raw data. Offline inspection/export does not require replaying command topics into a robot network.

nodes.label: Flashed Firmware Identity
nodes.rationale: Record reviewed source separately from flashed commit/binary hash evidence, board revision, USB identity, Agent environment/domain, motor compatibility, and boot/RC verification. A laptop checkout or USB descriptor does not establish the board binary. Fields remain null until evidenced, and an IMU profile does not establish motor/navigation function.

nodes.label: Geometry Load Measurements
nodes.rationale: Measure actual wheel radius, loaded effective radius, contact-center track, footprint, clearance, total/payload mass, and caster geometry with methods and per-measurement uncertainty. Effective radius inferred from displacement and rotation assumes sufficiently little slip. CAD, TF, caster observations, and COM estimates retain their distinct evidence labels.

nodes.label: Acquisition Profile Scope
nodes.rationale: The IMU-only profile requires /imu/data and /motor_status for USB/IMU inventory; the full profile retains broader required channels plus raw motor channels. A separate narrow contract does not rescue a failed full dataset. /imu/debug cannot replace valid IMU, and --check does not verify firmware identity, physical validity, QoS, or readiness.

nodes.label: Firmware Compatibility Uncertainty
nodes.rationale: Reference firmware commit 0d32593988cc817311d3dfdd8683df1f1b444a2c is reviewed source rather than a verified board binary. Its motor task invokes RobStride rs_ext paths on separate CAN buses, while the operator identifies Nino motors as CyberGear. README/source boot and timing differences remain uncertainty rather than proof of deployed behavior.

nodes.label: USB micro ROS Transport
nodes.rationale: STM32 sensor/CAN data travels through USB CDC and the bidirectional micro-ROS Agent into raw ROS channels for collection, audit, and bridge. Collector observation does not make Agent unidirectional. Bridge allow_motor_enable=false blocks its own enable service rather than direct ROS topics, firmware arbitration, or RC. Avoid duplicate Agents on the serial device.

nodes.label: Aggregate Wheel Response
nodes.rationale: The minimum claim uses final /cmd_vel, /motor_fb, and /motor_status to measure aggregate request-to-reported-wheel behavior, including transport, firmware, ramp/mode, and wheel mechanics. It cannot isolate motor PI latency without target telemetry. Straight equal-wheel references do not distinguish swapped left/right channels. Broader chain claims require every actual stage to be required.

nodes.label: Read Only Acquisition
nodes.rationale: The collector records existing drivers without launching control or sending motor commands. rosbag2 and audit run in separate processes so audit conversion is outside the recording callback. --check validates an offline plan without ROS or output creation. Capture budgets and clean closure do not grant motion authority.

nodes.label: Receipt Clock Semantics
nodes.rationale: The bag stores recorder receipt timestamps and original message headers inside CDR. Audit adds its own monotonic/ROS receipt clocks; it does not add monotonic time to every bag sample. Twist has no source header. Multi-host age subtraction requires clock origins, offsets, synchronization, and uncertainty before being called latency.

nodes.label: Signal Classification
nodes.rationale: Separate requested command, limited/executed reference, encoder feedback, and independent body motion. Channels are command, estimate, measured, or reported_unverified. /cmd_vel does not supply executed wheel targets; effort is not automatically measured torque. PI rate, publication rate, hardware sampling, source stamps, and receipt clocks have different meanings.

nodes.label: Unknown Metadata Convention
nodes.rationale: Unknown or unmeasured metadata remains null rather than zero, false, or empty text. Use SI units, explicit frames, actual component IDs, and measurement/config/operator provenance. The form is metadata rather than runtime configuration. Only a JSON object and nonempty session_id are enforced; the full field conventions are not an implemented JSON Schema.

nodes.label: Versioned Session Annotation
nodes.rationale: Actual session conditions, failures, interventions, outcomes, and split assignments require evidence. Preserve hashed original metadata and add a separate version such as session.annotated.json for post-run findings. Do not rewrite conditions retrospectively or relabel previously inspected/tuned data as an unseen held-out test.

nodes.label: Actuator Mode Arbitration
nodes.rationale: The reference source selects velocity mode through /cmd_vel and operation-control/MIT through /cmd_mit or /cmd_torque. Do not interleave modes or stack external velocity PI over the motor velocity PI. RC can affect effective permission independently of Pi bridge settings. Collection does not change arbitration or test watchdog behavior.

nodes.label: Motor Status Semantics
nodes.rationale: At the pinned reference source, status bits 0/1 denote left/right freshness, 2/3 CAN bus-off, 4 firmware enable, 5 timeout, and 6 MIT mode. Target publication rates are not measured rates. Status enable is not power/torque evidence; repeated JointState samples do not ensure fresh CAN feedback, and effort remains reported/unverified.

nodes.label: Failure Censoring
nodes.rationale: Retain aborts, timeout, missing samples, spikes, endpoint nonattainment, and right-censored response windows. Do not replace unknown metrics with zero, redefine endpoints after fitting, or silently retry/increase sample count. source_sequence_completed only reports helper sequence completion; encoder/body disagreement remains physically unknown rather than an assumed slip event.

nodes.label: Fresh Enable Acknowledgement
nodes.rationale: A pre-existing enable bit is not a fresh ACK. Proposed helper startup disables gate, sends zero, requests firmware disable, observes a later disabled status, holds zero, then requests enable and requires a new enabled status. Firmware g_system_enabled precedes RC arbitration and can differ from effective_enable; ACK does not prove physical motor permission.

nodes.label: Preregistered Response Metrics
nodes.rationale: Define baseline noise, sustained onset, settling, T90 endpoint, sampling resolution, gap/coverage, and invalid/abort rules before trials. T90 from ramp start includes ramp duration and is not transport latency or a motor time constant. Nominal geometry-derived wheel endpoints are not executed-target telemetry. Wheel settling is not independently measured body stopping.

nodes.label: ObservationAssembler causal sample validation
nodes.rationale: Caches IMU, wheels, commands and explicit health; preserves source and receipt times; rejects duplicate/reversed samples; checks required inputs and ages; applies a configured yaw rotation and retains sample provenance. This is not a fully calibrated 3D IMU transform.

nodes.label: Source, receipt, monotonic and simulation clock distinctions
nodes.norm_label: source, receipt, monotonic and simulation clock distinctions
nodes.rationale: A Twist bag timestamp does not establish motor application time. Receipt-based response delay combines transport, shaping and actuator response. Raw IMU timestamps are preserved, while the legacy wheel/odometry sanitizer may repair invalid stamps; retain raw channels to distinguish these effects.

nodes.label: Nino differential-drive robot and package responsibilities
nodes.norm_label: nino differential-drive robot and package responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Two driven wheels and two passive casters; Pi 5, STM32H7, USB micro-ROS and CAN motors. nino_description supplies models/worlds, nino_control control/history/projection, nino_rl tasks/learners/audits and nino_pi collection/QC/Studio. Reference firmware and package presence do not prove an active binary or launch.

nodes.label: Physical sensor channels and derived ROS estimates
nodes.norm_label: physical sensor channels and derived ros estimates
nodes.rationale: /imu/data and /motor_fb originate at STM32; the bridge republishes IMU and renamed wheel joints, computes encoder odometry, and an EKF may produce /odom. /scan_raw and deskewed /scan are not independent lasers. Raw left_wheel/right_wheel names differ from bridge left_wheel_joint/right_wheel_joint.

nodes.norm_label: geometric path versus timed trajectory scoring

nodes.norm_label: sensor-only controller versus privileged scoring boundary

nodes.norm_label: limits of encoder, gyro, accelerometer and horizontal lidar evidence
nodes.rationale: Wheel rotation is not independent body motion or longitudinal slip; gyro does not measure forward speed; acceleration includes gravity/mounting effects; horizontal LiDAR cannot preview every low obstacle. Endpoint ruler measurements establish displacement with uncertainty, without time-resolved onset, stopping or slip.

nodes.norm_label: compare task success before tracking and comfort
nodes.rationale: A stopped or failed robot can have low RMSE. Reports separate all episodes from successful episodes and require compatible task configuration, seeds, counts and perturbation mode; incomplete evaluations cannot be compared as full runs.

nodes.norm_label: unknown traversable obstacle and path-following research direction
nodes.rationale: The selected objective replaces known-route preview vibration reduction. Controller inputs are IMU, encoders, history and reference; ground truth, contact and obstacle metadata are reserved for scoring. Vibration and slip are secondary outcomes. nodes.norm_label: unknown-step traversal, tracking, goal and stop
nodes.rationale: Vibration, discrepancy and saturation are secondary diagnostics; holding nominal speed or reducing vibration alone does not establish task completion.

nodes.norm_label: b0, reactive b1, history and residual td3 roles
nodes.rationale: An untrained TD3 policy need not beat classical control before training, and a smoke run cannot establish convergence or learned benefit.

Residual TD3 is a bounded velocity-reference candidate after task/environment validation; PPO is optional. Qualify the environment before optimizer work, then compare trained policies against appropriate baselines.

nodes.label: Deployable controller versus privileged scoring boundary
nodes.norm_label: deployable controller versus privileged scoring boundary
nodes.rationale: IMU/encoder disturbance signals arrive after physical interaction begins; they are neither preview nor ground-truth first contact.
nodes.summary: Controller may know route and goal and use causal IMU, wheel encoders, command history, freshness and estimator. Step position, geometry, contact schedule and GT remain in separate scoring/audit channels. Start with 20 features × 5 frames; omit Common103 planned-stop features.

nodes.label: Hidden development/validation/test layout bank
nodes.rationale: A fixed step position can be learned from elapsed time or progress even without an obstacle_x feature. Feature-name guards alone do not prove provenance or remove shortcuts.
nodes.summary: Begin with the rigid Ø6 mm development family; vary hidden position and include clear floor. Lock splits by complete run/layout/seed before checkpoint selection. Test that changing obstacle metadata with identical sensor history leaves controller packets unchanged.

nodes.label: Physical success, explicit failure and UNKNOWN
nodes.norm_label: physical success, explicit failure and unknown
nodes.rationale: Estimator arrival and aggregate reward cannot substitute for physical task success or conceal failure.
nodes.summary: Success requires body arrival, full-robot geometric clearance and continuous stop. Keep failure, timeout, stall and override in the denominator; missing measurement is UNKNOWN. Report outcomes before tracking/time. Numeric tolerances and budget remained unset.

nodes.label: box_c1_6mm_dr historical training scenario
nodes.rationale: One rigid cylindrical C1 obstacle on a solid box floor; friction 0.85–1.15, obstacle X 0.55–0.75 m and radius 2.5–3.5 mm. Straight path endpoint is 3 m with 0.20 m/s cruise, alternating 6/8 s source stops and a 0.95 m local marker. Marker success is not endpoint or 6.45 m factory-goal arrival.

nodes.label: common103_v2 planned-stop 103D/1D contract
nodes.rationale: Appends remaining scheduled-stop time, common-window state and previous effective scalar to 100D history. This historical trained task uses scheduled stops and a local progress marker; its success flag does not establish unknown-obstacle goal arrival.

nodes.label: Current TD3 action: bounded common wheel-linear correction
nodes.norm_label: current td3 action: bounded common wheel-linear correction
nodes.rationale: One scalar a in [-1,1] requests equal corrections b*a on both wheels: b=0.02 m/s for obstacle/DR and 0.005 m/s for clear floor. Differential correction is zero. Valid history, permission, sensors, steady forward motion and the planned withdrawal window govern effective authority.

nodes.label: Generic two-action common/differential velocity residual
nodes.rationale: The separate generic ABI maps normalized common/differential proposals through an L1 normalizer to bounded left/right wheel-linear corrections. It is distinct from the current one-action common103_v2 trainer.

nodes.label: Causal wheel/gyro pose estimator and classical follower
nodes.norm_label: causal wheel/gyro pose estimator and classical follower
nodes.rationale: Integrates wheel-derived forward speed and gyro-Z yaw rate from causal samples, with explicit initial scenario pose rather than GT readback. The current Sim adapter follows one straight segment and supplies yaw control. Nav2 and the Pi EKF are separate implementations.

nodes.label: ReactiveGovernor classical state machine
nodes.rationale: Uses disturbance, angular-rate and wheel-error proxies with CRUISE, optional DELAY, HOLD, RECOVER, optional STALL and latched FAILSAFE. The common103_v2 trainer uses governor=False by default. Historical scale 0.90 and disabled generic 0.70 YAML are distinct settings; predictive risk/action ranking remains unvalidated.

nodes.label: Simulation wheel velocity PI and torque limits
nodes.norm_label: simulation wheel velocity pi and torque limits
nodes.rationale: effort_drive maps body references to wheel targets and bounded torque using Kp 0.30, Ki 0.10 and conditional anti-windup. Representative settings include 4 Nm PI contribution, 10 Nm/s slew, 12 rad/s² target acceleration, 500 Hz callback target, 10 Hz policy and 1 ms physics. The active velocity backend sets accept_torque=false.

nodes.label: TD3 deterministic MLP learner and effective job settings
nodes.norm_label: td3 deterministic mlp learner and effective job settings
nodes.rationale: The inspected CPU learner uses twin critics, delayed actor/target updates, smoothing, 256x256 networks, learning rate 0.0003, gamma 0.99, tau 0.005, batch 256, replay 100,000, fresh warmup 10,000 and policy delay 2. Effective profile and model builder determine the job. Deployment uses the deterministic actor, without real exploration or critic optimization.

nodes.label: 9 November interrupted common103_v2 checkpoint at 40,860 steps
nodes.norm_label: 9 november interrupted common103_v2 checkpoint at 40,860 steps
nodes.rationale: The inspected failed continuation saved 30k, 40k and 40,860 checkpoints, with 30,858 optimizer cycles and replay size 40,860. A 56 ms wheel source lag exceeded the 40 ms boundary requirement before final evaluation. This is the 9 November snapshot, preceding the README's later 50k failed-evaluation report.

nodes.label: 10 November common103_v2 seed11 reached 50k and failed evaluation
nodes.norm_label: 10 november common103_v2 seed11 reached 50k and failed evaluation

nodes.label: FeatureHistory: five actual 20-feature frames at 10 Hz
nodes.norm_label: featurehistory: five actual 20-feature frames at 10 hz
nodes.rationale: Five oldest-to-newest frames form a flattened 100D MLP input spanning 0.4 seconds; there is no LSTM. Padding does not earn history validity. Gaps, reversal and duplicates require refilling a valid epoch. Features include reference, wheels, gyro, gravity-retaining acceleration, command/residual history, ages and consistency proxies.

nodes.label: ResidualReference request-to-accepted reference projection
nodes.rationale: Enforces speed, yaw, wheel, acceleration, freshness, permission and stop/fault bounds. A zero baseline cannot initiate motion through residual alone. Accepted contribution is measured against a baseline projected from the same previous reference so ramp shaping is not credited to policy. Projection does not prove physical execution or safety.

nodes.label: Requested-action replay semantics
nodes.rationale: Projection belongs to the environment transition. Replay stores observation, requested action, reward, next observation and done; it does not silently replace the requested action with the accepted action. Windowed, projected and executed quantities are traced separately. Evaluation disables action noise and optimizer updates.

nodes.label: CommonScoreV2 nominal tracking reward
nodes.rationale: Uses GT velocity/yaw error against an independently shaped zero-residual nominal reference, requested-action regularization while the window is open and terminal penalties. It has no direct per-step path, slip or IMU-impact penalty. The 9 November unknown-step reward discussion is prospective and is superseded by later task implementation reports.

nodes.label: Historical Actuator Recording Gap
nodes.rationale: Historical run_logged_real.sh omitted /cmd_torque, /motor_enable, /cmd_mit, /scan_raw, and /collision_monitor_state. Controller total is a calculated command rather than measured torque or firmware receipt. Stale inputs, TF extrapolation, and EKF timing faults require causal timing analysis without changing stamps or deadlines to hide faults.

nodes.label: Logging V2 Preparation
nodes.rationale: run_logged_real_v2.sh was prepared and syntax checked to add missing actuator and guard channels. Recording with it was not run; it is an augmented historical navigation runner rather than a released velocity diagnostic helper. A proposed 0.05 m/s, 0.10 m/s², 2 s source, 60 s bag diagnostic precedes any bounded repeats.

nodes.label: SAC80k Session Evidence
nodes.rationale: Eight historical sessions used SAC80k torque. Six integrity-valid bags contain 313,555 messages: one Nav2 SUCCEEDED, three ABORTED, two without goals. Two corrupt bags remain diagnostic. Nav2 status and AMCL error do not establish physical arrival, stopping, comparative benefit, or TD3 deployment. All operator outcomes remain null.

nodes.label: Sensor Only Restore
nodes.rationale: A historical sensor-only window restored Agent, raw sensors, bridge, EKF, and required sensor TF while isolating bridge enable. It observed approximately 47 Hz IMU/wheel/status and 7 Hz scans. No actuator publishers, AMCL map TF, active Collision Monitor, or live STOP validation were present. Observed rates and ages are not latency guarantees.

nodes.label: IMU Frame Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Prepared collectors use LEVEL, NOSE_UP, and LEFT_SIDE_UP with raw CDR, numeric IMU, header/receipt times, status, and pinned hashes. Evaluation compares four coarse yaw candidates and retains unknown for weak signals or clock faults. No manual capture occurred. Level gravity alone cannot distinguish yaw 0 from +90 degrees.

nodes.label: Isolated Guard Qualification
nodes.rationale: Installed FootprintApproach passed five isolated diagnostic cases: live scan, synthetic clear, obstacle zero, clear rearm, and stale-source zero after timeout. Its output was never connected to firmware /cmd_vel. The monitor was subsequently deactivated and closed; this establishes integration behavior rather than physical stopping or an active motor guard.

nodes.label: Post Reboot USB Absence
nodes.rationale: At the final post-reboot probe, STM32 and LiDAR USB devices were absent, Agent waited for serial, and the LiDAR driver exited. The probe received no sensor samples or odom TF despite bridge/EKF processes. Final sensor readiness and motion readiness were false, authority was zero, and the cause of USB absence remained unknown.

nodes.label: Velocity SysID Recording Profile
nodes.rationale: The prepared recording profile declares firmware_velocity_reference and requires raw IMU, wheel feedback, status, /scan, /tf_static, and final /cmd_vel after capture. Torque/MIT messages fail its velocity-only contract, including zero requests. Optional event channels stay optional without fake messages. It retains motion_released=false and does not enable or generate trajectories.

nodes.label: Mounting Contract Divergence
nodes.rationale: The Pi SAC branch has a 23D observation, torque residual, and identity IMU mounting, whereas the repository TD3/history branch has another ABI/action contract and earlier evidence used approximate offsets with yaw +90 degrees. Configuration differences require firmware/frame/mounting reconciliation rather than overwriting historical evidence.

nodes.label: Native Velocity Reference Backend
nodes.rationale: The next real SysID campaign selects firmware velocity mode because the intended TD3 controller adjusts bounded velocity references. The proposed chain passes shaping and Collision Monitor before /cmd_vel and the motor velocity loop. It was not run during restoration. Pi torque PI and historical SAC torque remain separate.

nodes.label: Immutable SQLite QC
nodes.rationale: Collector and QC now compare per-topic metadata counts, accept only closed SQLite storage through immutable readers, and reject nonempty WAL/journal. Offline recheck preserved six valid/two failed historical bags and 431 sealed file hashes. Forty-six offline tests passed, including synthetic Parquet export; none created new physical data or repaired corrupt bags.

nodes.label: Command Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Manual or Nav2 source enters the initially disabled command_gate, then /cmd_vel_selected, velocity_smoother, /cmd_vel_smoothed, Collision Monitor using scan/TF, and final /cmd_vel to the real backend. The package does not supply real motor/sensor drivers. Initial YAML limits are not hardware calibration.

nodes.label: Gate Stop Latch
nodes.rationale: Software stop latches the gate; reset requires disable followed by reset_stop and does not automatically enable. Keyboard expiry and gate timeout depend on the functioning software chain and do not replace motor watchdog or physical stop. Mode switching clears gate commands but does not cancel a Nav2 action.

nodes.label: SSH Operator Workflow
nodes.rationale: laptop_control.py and its shell wrapper run Pi keyboard/control commands through SSH; laptop ROS networking is optional for RViz. The collector runs separately in the verified driver domain. Recording precedes enable, driving ends before recording, and recording continues through settling. Stopping the collector does not stop the robot.

nodes.label: Command Ownership
nodes.rationale: Use the real driver's verified domain and audit all command-stage publishers. Launch-time duplicate-stack checks are snapshots rather than distributed locks. Do not run keyboard and joystick on the same teleop topic or competing publishers directly to final /cmd_vel. Publication ownership must remain valid during the actual trial.

nodes.label: Localization Authority
nodes.rationale: Mapping and navigation must avoid duplicate command stacks and map-to-odom owners. Navigation uses a real measured occupancy map stored on Pi after mapping/SLAM stops; helper launch neither enables nor sends a goal. Goal/route metadata is needed because /goal_pose is not a complete action-goal log.

nodes.label: Motion Release Contract
nodes.rationale: A new protocol must explicitly confirm owners, RC selection/arm/stop, backend, bounds, clocks, abort rules, and operator readiness. Generic templates and --check do not enforce or grant release. Historical V1/V2 slots remain closed; the draft six-trial design is not granted budget. Software preparation creates no physical evidence.

nodes.label: Endpoint Measurement
nodes.rationale: A proposed fixed body marker and floor datum measured before/after by tape can establish endpoint displacement with resolution and repeatability uncertainty. Wheel visibility is recorded separately. Endpoints provide no body time series, onset, T90, instantaneous speed, post-zero stopping distance, or slip ratio. The diagnostic has not been executed.

nodes.label: LiDAR Reference Candidate
nodes.rationale: LiDAR-only scan matching in a structured scene is proposed as a body trajectory/heading estimator, with endpoint checks and declared fusion. Historical approximately 7 Hz scans do not establish suitability for approximately 100 ms transients, contact, pitch, or feature-poor scenes. Endpoint validation does not validate every trajectory point.

nodes.label: Camera Optional Acquisition
nodes.rationale: The operator has no camera. Camera absence does not block acquisition contracts, observation history, reported-wheel identification, or zero-authority shadow. History still requires correct adapter ABI, frames, freshness, and causality. Physical body/slip claims require a suitable independent reference, which may use another measurement method.

nodes.label: Claim Specific Quality
nodes.rationale: Raw integrity, reported-wheel usability, endpoint usability, validated trajectory, and measurable slip are distinct quality claims. Studio remains capped at WARN/Q2 rather than automatically promoting tape measurements to Q3/Q4. A dedicated manual endpoint entry workflow was not yet implemented; annotations belong in separate derived records.

nodes.label: Independent Body Reference
nodes.rationale: Independent body measurements distinguish wheel rotation from body displacement, speed, slip, stopping, and navigation error. Encoder-derived odometry is not independent body truth. A measurement must match the claimed quantity and declare geometry, timing, fusion, uncertainty, and validation limits.

nodes.label: Capture Completeness
nodes.rationale: captured_not_calibrated means required samples, readable closed storage, and completed acquisition processes, rather than calibrated sensors, timing accuracy, physical success, or safety. Missing required data stays incomplete. Counts do not establish packet loss or coverage without an independent production count. Raw failures, timestamps, outliers, and unknown values are preserved.

nodes.label: Laya statistical interpretation advisory
nodes.rationale: Supports interpretation of statistics; does not train the actor, implement control, certify safety or choose a winner against evaluation evidence.

nodes.label: Separate real nino_real_rl PI/SAC torque backend
nodes.norm_label: separate real nino_real_rl pi/sac torque backend
nodes.rationale: The reviewed Pi controller adds two SAC wheel-torque residuals to external wheel PI, then publishes /cmd_torque through the STM32 MIT path. It uses 23D observations, two actions, 0.30 Nm residual bound and 2 Nm software total bound. This does not validate the TD3 velocity contract.

nodes.label: 9 November Pi sensor reconnection and observer-readiness snapshot
nodes.norm_label: 9 november pi sensor reconnection and observer-readiness snapshot
nodes.rationale: A second 12-second probe observed sensors but receipt gaps up to about 345 ms. Five isolated Collision Monitor diagnostics passed and the monitor was subsequently closed. Studio discovery missed tf_static despite longer TF lookup success; the prepared QoS probe failed to execute after network loss. Remote liveness remained unverified and no new motion dataset started.

nodes.label: Combined Nino Studio collection, training and evidence interface
nodes.norm_label: combined nino studio collection, training and evidence interface
nodes.rationale: Provides read-only recording with metadata/QC/export, Sim smoke/research training and checkpoint continuation, map/trajectory and episode/checkpoint monitoring, and historical evidence/to-do views. Historical evidence and live worker status are distinct.

nodes.label: Command ownership, firmware modes and recorder independence
nodes.norm_label: command ownership, firmware modes and recorder independence
nodes.rationale: Real velocity requests pass MCU arbitration/watchdog and CAN motor references. Torque/MIT/velocity topics can change mode when interleaved. The Pi helper chain is keyboard/Nav2, gate, smoother, Collision Monitor and final command. Recording does not enable motion, and ending recording does not stop another process's controller; installed FootprintApproach and older StopZone configurations have distinct provenance.

nodes.label: Raw-session integrity and timing QC
nodes.rationale: Require normal bag closure, decoding/SQLite integrity, matching counts, hashes and provenance; explicitly report missing/nonfinite channels, reversed/duplicate clocks, gaps and interventions. Missing values remain missing. Observed rates do not prove packet loss, and Q2 integrity is not Q3/Q4 body, benefit or deployment validation.

nodes.label: Simulation and Pi geometry declarations are not calibrated equivalence
nodes.norm_label: simulation and pi geometry declarations are not calibrated equivalence
nodes.rationale: Sim wheel radius/separation are 0.0625 m and 0.34273666 m versus Pi declarations 0.060 m and 0.345 m. Current Pi IMU TF is identity/zero, differing from historical yaw evidence. Declared TF, rolling radius, modeled mass/caster clearance and physical measurements are distinct.

nodes.label: Selected real velocity backend: STM32 to motor internal loop
nodes.norm_label: selected real velocity backend: stm32 to motor internal loop
nodes.rationale: The reference /cmd_vel path selects velocity mode, converts body velocity to wheel speeds and sends CAN references to the motor's internal velocity loop. Firmware source acceleration/current declarations are not readback of the flashed binary or physical motor configuration.

nodes.label: TD3 Sim-to-real adapter and evidence requirements
nodes.norm_label: td3 sim-to-real adapter and evidence requirements
nodes.rationale: Real TD3 velocity authority requires matching observation/action ABI, mapping, export, firmware mode/owner qualification, measured backend dynamics and hardware tests. Separate SAC torque experiments and sensor bags do not validate this controller. Independent body-speed/slip reference and accepted velocity-backend SysID remain unresolved.
